# Export documents

::: {.doc-lead}
Choose a file format, apply a journal style, keep citations live in Word, and install what Quarto exports need.
:::

## Export {#export}

The **Export** button in the status bar, or **Alt+E**, opens a dialog with two independent
choices: the **file format** (**PDF**, **Word**, **HTML**) and the **journal style**. An
**Engine** line says what will do the work, and **Output** shows where the file will land.

| Format | Engine | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PDF** | Flux's in-app renderer — fast, nothing to install | Figures, captions, panel references and the bibliography are resolved by Flux. |
| **HTML** | Flux's in-app renderer | Embedded slides keep their playback. |
| **Word** | Quarto | Needs Quarto; the dialog offers **Install Quarto…** when it is missing (no admin rights needed). Journal styles and **Live Zotero citations** are available here. |

- Every format saves where you choose, defaulting to the project's `exports/` folder. The
  suggested file name follows the format you pick, so switching to Word suggests a `.docx`
  name; a name you typed yourself is kept. **Change…** picks another location.
- A long render shows its progress and can be cancelled.
- Figure renders, captions and panel references are resolved during export. A failure
  appears as a notification that names what to fix.
- The app exports the document you have open. From a terminal, `flux compile` exports the
  project's default document (or `--doc path.qmd`) through Quarto to PDF, HTML or Word; see
  [Command line](/docs/cli.html).

### Journal styles {#journal-styles}

The **Style** menu offers **Flux house style** (the default manuscript look), **Nature** and
**Nature Communications**. Choosing a journal makes the exported file follow that journal's house
style: how figure and panel references read (`Fig. 1a,b`; Nature Communications spaces the list,
`Fig. 1a, b`), how citations are marked (superscript numerals, before the punctuation), how
reference entries are built (all authors up to five, then `et al.`), what order the sections
appear in, and the submission formatting a manuscript needs (12pt Times, double-spaced,
line-numbered).

In the app, journal styles apply to **Word** export: with PDF or HTML selected and a journal
chosen, the dialog says *Journal styles are available for Word export only* and waits until you
switch to Word. Nature prefers Word for submission anyway, and a journal-styled `.docx` needs no
TeX. A journal-styled **PDF** is available from the terminal —
`flux compile --to pdf --style nature` — and runs through Quarto and LaTeX, which needs the
[PDF dependencies](#pdf-dependencies) below.

**Your writing never changes.** The editor keeps Flux's own conventions no matter which
journal is selected — chips, figure references and caption leads look the same whether you
are aiming at Nature or nowhere. Only the exported file and the preview follow the journal,
so switching journals is instant, and switching back loses nothing. Nothing is rewritten in
your manuscript on disk: a journal style is a lens on the way out, not an edit.

Selecting a style is remembered per project, and agents can use the same one from the
terminal with `flux compile --to docx --style nature`.

### Live Zotero citations in Word {#live-zotero-citations}

With **Word** selected, tick **Live Zotero citations** and the citations arrive in the `.docx`
as real Zotero fields rather than plain text, so whoever opens the file in Word can refresh
them, change the citation style, renumber after an edit, and add their own citations beside
yours. Leave it unticked and the citations are ordinary text, which is fine for a file nobody
will edit.

Each live citation travels with its full reference details, so it works on any machine, even one
that has never seen your library. If a co-author already sent you Word files written with
Zotero, **Link to library from…** takes those files and matches your citations against the works
in them; the ones they already have arrive attached to their own library entries instead of as
separate copies, and the dialog says how many matched. Anything unmatched still works; it simply
is not linked to anything.

One boundary: a citation inside a footnote stays ordinary text rather than becoming a live
field — the export tells you when that happened. Citations in the body, in figure captions and
in the reference list are all live. From the terminal the same options are
`flux compile --to docx --zotero-fields [--zotero-library a.docx,b.docx]`. Syncing your library
from Zotero is a separate feature; see [Zotero](/docs/zotero.html).

### Journal Check {#journal-check}

**Alt+J** opens **Journal Check**, which reads your manuscript against the selected
journal's rulebook: title and summary-paragraph length, headings the journal doesn't print
(Nature uses neither "Introduction" nor "Results"), missing sections like Data availability,
word budgets, display-item and reference caps, and typed-out figure references that don't
match house style. Click any item to jump to it.

It is **advice, and never blocks an export** — Nature itself says style and length won't
influence consideration at first submission. Switch the panel to *Accepted / final* and the
sections a journal requires at acceptance become warnings rather than notes.

One deliberate limit: Flux formats references it owns — the ones you insert as figure
references — and only *points at* figure references you typed by hand. It cannot tell your
"Figure 2, panel D" from a mention of someone else's Figure 2D, so it never rewrites your
prose.

## PDF dependencies {#pdf-dependencies}

Flux's own PDF export ships inside the app (as do its video encoder and the offline help) and
needs neither Quarto nor TeX. Quarto powers **Word** export and `flux compile` (HTML, Word,
PDF; it bundles its own pandoc), and Quarto's PDF builds additionally need TeX. Without TeX,
`flux compile --to pdf` fails while HTML and Word still work.

**Set up Flux** (**Settings → General → Setup**, or **Ctrl+K → Set up Flux…**) installs
both: Quarto into `~/FluxConfig`, and TinyTeX through Quarto in your home folder. A Quarto you
installed yourself — on your `PATH` or in its usual install folder — always wins over Flux's
copy, and `quarto install tinytex` adds TeX to it. Nothing here needs admin rights.

**TinyTeX is not added to your PATH.** It installs into `~/Library/TinyTeX` (macOS) or
`~/.TinyTeX` (Linux). Flux and Quarto find it anyway, so exports work without any shell change,
but TeX's own commands (`tlmgr`, `kpsewhich`, used below) need it on your PATH:

```bash
# macOS — add to ~/.zshrc to make it permanent
export PATH="$HOME/Library/TinyTeX/bin/universal-darwin:$PATH"
# Linux — add to ~/.bashrc
export PATH="$HOME/.TinyTeX/bin/x86_64-linux:$PATH"
```

### Extras for a journal-styled PDF {#journal-pdf-extras}

`flux compile --to pdf --style nature` asks LaTeX for things a minimal install may not have:
line numbers, double spacing, a Times-compatible font, and a way to place Flux's SVG figures in a
PDF. How you add them depends on how TeX got onto the machine:

| TeX install | Command | Needs admin? |
|---|---|---|
| TinyTeX (the setup window, or `quarto install tinytex`) | `tlmgr install lineno setspace` | No — TinyTeX lives in your home directory |
| MacTeX | `sudo tlmgr install lineno setspace` | Yes |
| Linux distro TeX Live (apt) | `sudo apt install texlive-latex-recommended texlive-humanities texlive-luatex texlive-fonts-recommended` | Yes — Debian and Ubuntu disable `tlmgr` package installs |

Figures also need **`rsvg-convert`** (`librsvg2-bin` on Debian and Ubuntu, `librsvg` on Homebrew
and Arch): Flux renders figures as SVG, and LaTeX cannot place those directly.

Check what you have (both commands need TinyTeX on your PATH, see above):

```bash
kpsewhich lineno.sty setspace.sty   # both should print a path
rsvg-convert --version              # needed for figures in PDF
quarto check                        # quarto + tinytex, if you export papers
```

None of this affects **Word**: a journal-styled `.docx` needs no TeX at all. When an export does
hit a missing piece, Flux names the package to install instead of showing you the raw LaTeX log.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| With **Word** selected, **Export** is disabled and the dialog says Word export needs Quarto | Quarto isn't installed → **Install Quarto…** in the dialog, or **Set up Flux → Word export · Quarto** |
| *Journal styles are available for Word export only* | A journal is chosen with PDF or HTML selected → switch to Word, or use `flux compile --to pdf --style nature` from a terminal |
| `flux compile --to pdf` fails; HTML works | No TeX → **Set up Flux → PDF through Quarto**, or `quarto install tinytex` |
| A journal PDF fails with `File 'lineno.sty' not found` (or `setspace.sty`) | Minimal TeX install → the table above |
| A journal PDF fails mentioning `rsvg-convert` | SVG figures cannot be placed → install `librsvg2-bin` / `librsvg` |
| A journal PDF fails with `luaotfload` or `not loadable: Metric` | lualatex is present but its fonts are not → `texlive-luatex` + `texlive-fonts-recommended`, or use TinyTeX |
| `kpsewhich` or `tlmgr`: command not found, yet exports work | TinyTeX is not on your PATH → add the line above; Flux and Quarto never needed it |
| A Word export says figures will be missing | No render could be produced for the named figures → open Figure so they load, then export again |
| A citation came out as plain text in a Zotero export | It sits in a footnote, which stays ordinary text → move it into the body if it must be live |
| Journal Check flags something you disagree with | It is advice and never blocks an export → dismiss it |
